Part 1 Project: The Fernhill Community Garden Theme

The project that closes Part 1 (Modules 1 to 4). Each learner builds a block theme, fernhill, for a client who is NOT Pages & Co.: the Fernhill Community Garden, a volunteer-run garden on Orchard Lane. Briefed and started in Session 7 (after Lesson 4.3), worked on at home, finished in the Session 8 studio, handed in one week after Session 8. About 3 hours 45 minutes of work for a learner who did the Part 1 lessons; nothing in it is new, everything is a lesson's skill applied to a new client. The timed Part 1 assessment (Session 8) is separate and tests the classic-theme side (Module 4) on its own.

Covers Modules 1–4Kickoff Session 7Studio Session 8Due 1 week after Session 8Met: 14/20, no row at 1
The client (Odette Marsh, volunteer coordinator, by email)

“Our website runs on a free theme from 2019 that nobody dares to touch. We would like our own theme, made for us: green and calm, our news on the front page three at a time, a big welcome at the top, a call for Saturday volunteers, and an autumn look we can switch on in October. Our volunteers write news and edit pages in the editor; none of us writes code. And please: nothing that breaks when WordPress updates itself.”

Fictional client, fictional people. The garden's own news is not written yet, so learners build and test on their course site's posts and pages: four posts (three of them in News), About Us, Events and Contact. The theme must not care whose content it shows.

Files (labs/module-08/p1-project/)
  • BRIEF.md: the learner's brief (this section in the learner's words: requirements, milestones, hand-in, rubric). Hand it out at the Session 7 kickoff.
  • fernhill_starter/: the starter theme. It activates and runs with no message; the self-check says Checks passed: 1 of 12. Ready-made: assets/css/fernhill.css, assets/images/leaf.svg, parts/header.html; half-made: patterns/hero.php (the model pattern, three strings left to translate, its category missing); TODOs in style.css, functions.php; a bare theme.json and templates/index.html.
  • test_fernhill.php: the self-check, 12 OK/TODO lines, one per testable piece of R1 to R7. Learners run it as often as they like (wp eval-file --use-include test_fernhill.php with fernhill active). It is a help, not the score: R8 and the rubric's quality rows are read by you.
  • fernhill_front.png: the model solution's front page on the course site (what done looks like; learners may see it).
  • fernhill_solution/: your model solution (Checks passed: 12 of 12 on the after:lesson_13 site, checked by python3 labs/check_labs.py module-08). Never handed out before the feedback.
Requirements (what the learner's BRIEF.md lists)
RequirementLessonsSelf-check
R1Design system. style.css names the theme: Theme Name Fernhill, Text Domain fernhill, Version 1.0.0, Requires at least 7.1, Requires PHP (the version you test on, at least 8.1), Tested up to 7.1. theme.json is version 3 with the 7.1 $schema and holds the design: exactly five colors named by role, in this order: base #f7f5ee, contrast #23301f, primary #3f6b35, secondary #e4ecd9, accent #9c4426 (defaultPalette off); content width 680px, wide width 1100px; a serif for text and a sans-serif for headings (system font stacks, no font files); links and buttons in primary, text in contrast on base.3.21 to 4
R2Templates and parts. Templates index, front-page, single and page (and 404, R7). Two template parts declared in theme.json with their areas: header (the site title and a Navigation block) and footer (two lines: "Fernhill Community Garden · 48 Orchard Lane · 555-0187" and "Workdays every Saturday, 9 a.m. to noon"). Every template is the header part (tagName header), one group with tagName main, and the footer part (tagName footer): the landmarks screen readers and the skip link need.3.1, 3.25, 6
R3Patterns and the front page. Two PHP patterns in patterns/: fernhill/hero (an h1 "Grow food, grow friendships", the welcome paragraph, a button "About the garden" to /about/, the leaf drawing assets/images/leaf.svg with its alt text) and fernhill/volunteer-call (an h2 "Volunteer on Saturday mornings", a paragraph, a button "Sign up for a workday" to /contact/ in the accent color). Both in the theme's category fernhill; every visible string through esc_html_e() or esc_attr_e() with the fernhill text domain; URLs through esc_url( home_url( ... ) ). front-page.html: the hero, an h2 "News from the garden", a Query Loop that inherits the main query (title, date, excerpt, pagination), the volunteer call.3.3, 1.37, 9
R4Style variation. styles/autumn.json, titled Autumn: the same five slugs with autumn colors (the brief suggests base #fbf4ea, contrast #3a2318, primary #8a3b1e, secondary #f1dfc6, accent #4f6b2a). Odette switches it on in Styles; nothing else changes.3.38
R5functions.php. Registers the pattern category fernhill (label "Fernhill Garden") on init, and enqueues assets/css/fernhill.css (shipped in the starter) with the handle fernhill-style, versioned with the theme's own Version, on wp_enqueue_scripts. One prefixed function (fernhill_) per job, each with a docblock.4.3, 2.37, 10
R6The main query. The blog home (the front page of this site, which shows the latest posts) lists three posts per page and paginates the rest (the fourth course post on /page/2/). Change the main query in pre_get_posts with the three guards of Lesson 4.2: not in the admin, the main query only, the blog home only. No second query in the template.4.211
R7404 page. templates/404.html: an h1 "This path is overgrown", one sentence, and a Search block, between the same header and footer. WordPress answers with status 404.3.112
R8Quality. No PHP message on any page with debugging on (debug.log stays quiet); WordPress coding standards (tabs, spaces inside parentheses, docblocks: Lesson 1.3); every function prefixed; no edits to core, the course themes or another theme's files; no Site Editor copies left in the database (Lesson 3.2: they win over your files); the per-URL check of Lesson 3.2 passes for /, /page/2/, /hello-world/, /about/, /category/news/, /?s=garden (200) and /no-such-path/ (404); a short NOTES.md in the theme folder.1.3, 3.2all

Stretch (not required; evidence for Exemplary): A section style (styles/sections/, Lesson 3.3) for the volunteer band instead of hand-set colors. search.html with a Query Title of the search type and the Query No Results block (Lesson 3.2). A child theme fernhill-kids for the children's garden page: Template: fernhill, a theme.json that only changes the accent color and one page-kids.html template (Lesson 3.4). screenshot.png (1200 by 900) so the theme looks right in Appearance > Themes.

225 minutes of solo work: about 35 in the Session 7 studio, 50 in the Session 8 studio, the rest (about 2 hours 20 minutes) at home between the sessions and in the week after Session 8. Learners who finish early take a stretch item.

Session 7 kickoff (what the Session 7 guide runs, about 35 minutes)
  • Read the brief together (5m). Odette's email aloud; then the requirement list on the slide. Ask: "Which module does each requirement come from?" (R1 to R4 Module 3, R5 and R6 Module 4, R8 every module.) Name the rule that matters most: the theme is a new folder; nothing in pagesco, the course's other themes or core changes.
  • M1 for everyone (10m). From the project folder: cp -r labs/module-08/p1-project/fernhill_starter wordpress/wp-content/themes/fernhill, wp theme activate fernhill, cp labs/module-08/p1-project/test_fernhill.php wordpress/, wp eval-file --use-include test_fernhill.php. Done = Checks passed: 1 of 12 on every screen. Then a two-minute tour of the starter: which files are ready, which are TODO, and hero.php as the model for R3.
  • M2 started (15 to 20m). The style.css header, then the palette in theme.json (copy the five slugs and hex values from the brief, in order). Run the self-check after each save: once the header, palette and layout widths are in, checks 1 to 4 turn OK (Checks passed: 4 of 12). Circulate for JSON commas (a trailing comma = a decode notice and no styles: Lesson 3.2 Mistake 1).
  • Close (2m). Due dates: M2 and M3 before Session 8 (about 1 hour 45 minutes at home); bring the theme and the last self-check output. And: wp theme activate pagesco when you stop for the day.
Rules for learners
  • Open book: the lesson pages, your notes, your workbook, your own course code (the pagesco theme is the closest model). Talk ideas through with other learners; write your own code.
  • AI assistants may explain an error message; they do not write the theme. Be ready to explain any line of it: the review in Session 8 and the feedback may ask.
  • Work on your course site. The test switches nothing: you activate fernhill yourself, and when you stop for the day you run wp theme activate pagesco (Session 9 and Lesson 5.1 start from pagesco active).
  • Edit the theme's FILES. If you try something in the Site Editor, export it or copy its markup into the file, then delete the database copy (Lesson 3.2, Mistake 3): a copy left behind hides your files and is not in your zip.
What learners hand in
  • One zip, fernhill-<yourname>.zip, of the theme folder wordpress/wp-content/themes/fernhill/ (the folder itself, not its parent), made on your computer.
  • NOTES.md in the theme folder: what is unfinished (or "nothing"); one decision you made and why (a color, a template, where a piece of code lives); the last lines of the self-check.
  • Due one week after Session 8, to the address your instructor gives you. Feedback comes back within a week, on the rubric below.

Met = at least 14 of 20 points with no row at 1. Below that, the learner revises once, within a week of the feedback.
